correctness.rationale: For twists below \(d\), Xu's weighted conormal sequence and the vanishing \(H^1(\mathcal O_S(k))=0\) identify surface one-forms with the kernel of the restricted weighted Euler map. In weighted degree \(t<d\), a relation in the hypersurface coordinate ring lifts to the polynomial ring. Since the coordinate variables form a regular sequence, their first syzygies are the Koszul relations; the least possible weighted degree is \(a_0+a_1\), and the displayed two-variable Koszul relation is nonzero at that degree. The finite package checker agrees for every ordered quadruple with weights at most six and for the \((2,3,5,7)\) Fermat example, but the proof is the regular-sequence argument.

originality.rationale: The exact threshold is mechanically implied by two already published ingredients. Xu's same-surface proof supplies the weighted Euler and conormal sequences and the all-twist line-bundle cohomology needed to identify \(H^0(\Omega_S^1(t))\) with the ambient Euler-kernel for \(t<d\). Araujo--Corrêa--Massarenti explicitly describe global twisted one-forms on weighted projective space as weighted homogeneous tuples \((F_i)\) satisfying \(\sum a_i z_iF_i=0\). For a polynomial ring, the first syzygies of the coordinate regular sequence are the standard Koszul relations, whose least weighted degree is immediately \(a_0+a_1\). Thus the final statement is an elementary implication of stronger published structural descriptions even though the number \(a_0+a_1\) is not printed as a theorem.

final_claim: For a well-formed quasi-smooth hypersurface \(S_d\subset\mathbb P(a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3)\) with ordered positive weights and \(d>\sum_i a_i\), the first twist carrying a nonzero reflexive one-form is \(a_0+a_1\), attained by the weighted Koszul form \(a_1x_1\,dx_0-a_0x_0\,dx_1\).
limitations: First reflexive one-forms only; no exact threshold for higher symmetric powers is claimed.
